notes.title: v0.11.0 Development Update - Part 1
notes.notes:
Hello, merchants!  

We have an even bigger development update this time around with our v0.11.0 build, which we will be splitting into 2 update posts. Here is part 1:


Combat System - Boost/Affliction


Our combat boost/affliction (renaming WIP) system has always been a WIP with more features on the to-do list, and now it has finally gone through the big update it was waiting for. 

Different Effects - we have changed and balanced the effects of each boost and affliction compared to our older builds, and also increased the amount.

Tier and Combination - boosts and afflictions can now be combined to higher tiers. We have introduced lower-tiered B/A for basic trading goods, which can also be combined into higher-tiered effects, allowing more strategising during combat and having access to more varied B/A with fewer goods.

Duration - Duration of most B/A now also lasts longer, with the average being 3 turns.

Negotiation - B/A also plays a role in our updated negotiation system, such as enemies having more afflictions will also contribute to being more disadvantaged, hence re-negotiating the battle from a disadvantaged position.

[img src="{STEAM_CLAN_IMAGE}/36017218/868edd4c774907617e1e933cb2d98be9880652e5.png"]
Negotiation System - New Features
We have implemented more features in our negotiation system.

In older builds, negotiation will pop up once at the start of combat, and that's it. It was always a work in progress, and now with v0.11.0 we have finally made big improvements.

Stages - negotiation will now also appear in different stages of combat, depending on how the battle is going. If you are winning the battle, the enemy may make a plea with a new negotiation offer, such as allowing them to escape, or even have them offer up some goods or coins. Conversely, a more costly negotiation may be at hand if you are instead losing the battle. 

New UI - The UI popup has been revised to be more compact and now shows more button descriptions

  [img src="{STEAM_CLAN_IMAGE}/36017218/844e31a9fdd7c4f179b3c6adc98cb815c0176426.png"]
Other Notable Improvements
Wilderness Travel - travel waiting time (in real time) has been reduced as frequently requested from playtesting feedback

Shop & Selling - drag and drop is now available for selling goods from your inventory.


Events & Demo
We were very thankful to have been able to participate in this year's #TurnBasedThursdayFest this month!

A notable game-crashing bug present in our demo this month has now been fixed. We apologise to all players who were affected while playing our demo. 


Content-Focused Development Ahead
From the completion of this build onwards, we will be soft-locking our gameplay mechanic development. 

What this means is we won't be making any more big changes to our gameplay mechanics and features (aside from adjustments and fixes based on feedback) in order to put our full focus on developing the rest of the content for our game. 

Look forward to our content updates!



Until next time,
Cynthia (Founder/Developer)

notes.title: v0.10.11 Development Update - Systems and Quality of Life
notes.notes:
Heya merchants!

We have a bigger update this time due to a longer dev cycle for this build, so enjoy!

Settlement & Environment
The following gameplay improvements have been made to the interactive elements in settlements and environments.

{STEAM_CLAN_IMAGE}/36017218/4e845efb0abd469b4a3765b55e9354522fffdf43.png
Many other improvements have been made according to player feedback to help with gameplay elements and quality of life, such as:

 Randomly Encountered Merchants - random merchants and traders met in settlements now are more full-fledged, meaning a better system at managing goods available for trading, and also retain their data in save games and are not just one-time randomly generated NPCs.
 Trader Types - These merchants are also split into two types: local traders and travelling traders. The main difference is that local traders are local settlers who will have the same needs at the settlement itself (e.g. the settlement itself is short on tools), while travelling traders are only stopping by and have their own very different needs and what they’re looking for.
 Move & Interact - We have made improvements to the pathfinding system so that when interacting with elements in the environment, only a single click is needed (as opposed to the old code, where another click to interact is needed)
 Rumours - Rumours from interacting with locals have improved by changing it so that most rumours will either reveal some info about trading goods value in another settlement or wilderness events nearby, as well as give a bit of merchant experience.


Combat System

 Game Over After Defeat - Defeat in combat used to take away some trading goods or coins and allow the player to continue on, but often than not, the amount of goods taken away is enough to set the player back to fail the job objective, hence leading to game over anyway. This has been changed back to the default game over in Story Mode, or retreat back to the merchant company in Company Mode.
 Bug Fixes - Various combat system bug fixes have also been made thanks to playtesting.


UI and Quality of Life
{STEAM_CLAN_IMAGE}/36017218/3ba05011ed1c938827b3ed7c04b88490975bdaad.png
 Minimap - A fully working minimap system has been implemented for every settlement, showing the player’s location in the settlement and nearby buildings of interest. This was a heavily requested addition from playtest feedback.
 Trading Goods UI - Each settlement now also has a UI element that shows the type of trading goods they produce and need next to the minimap
 Hide/Reveal UI - The minimap, objective UI, and trading goods UI can all be toggled to hide or reveal with a click at the player’s discretion.
 World Map - The world map has also been improved with better UI labels for objectives and events, as well as UI pointers added to show the distance between settlements relative to the player’s current position. These were also a requested addition from feedback and should’ve been implemented much earlier, but were easy to miss for us developers.


Content & Timeline

We have also been working hard behind the scenes with assets and content development (many of which will be a secret until release)
Another good news is that we have finally locked in a solid release window for the game based on our development timeline. More news will be announced in the coming months!

Until next time,
Cynthia

notes.title: v0.10.10 Development Update - New Year & Progress
notes.notes:
Hey all, we hope everyone has had a great start to 2025! 

Here at Thousand Tonic, we've been so busy lately that I've been pushing back from writing a development update, but enough procrastination, here's how things have been progressing along!

v0.10.10 is the build we worked on post-PAX Aus, and it features:

Gameplay & Quality of Life

The rogue-lite system now operates on what's called Merchant Exp, allowing various actions and successes (such as good bartering or overcoming hostiles) to gain exp for the player. Once enough exp is accumulated, a rogue-lite boost or Merchant Focus is granted. This applies to both Story and Company game modes.

Many other improvements have been made according to player feedback to help with gameplay elements and quality of life, such as:

 Moving and automatically entering buildings / interacting with NPCs when clicked on
 Rumours giving specific discoveries + merchant exp
 Improved wilderness events, better choices
 Combat defeat is game over (as before, the setback from defeat was already enough to game over the player).

New Art Assets

A preview of our new Relic City environment art, implemented along with other new art assets.

{STEAM_CLAN_IMAGE}/36017218/ee00d88f20d5cafda4788afa56271149a34ef6bc.png

notes.title: v0.10.7 Development Update
notes.notes:
I hope everyone is off to a great start in 2024! 

We have been hard at work since our last build, and have taken in all the feedback from our players to redesign and improve our game systems. Here is a preview of what we're currently working on:

Combat System

Some of the major feedback we have received regarding the old combat system includes:

 The current combat system is too basic. Need more actions and more ways to attack.
 More RPG elements like in other turn-based RPG combat systems
 More interaction with the rest of the game, such as weather, more emphasis on nighttime, other items, and weapons?
 Be able to control the guards separately as well. More notable guard abilities.

{STEAM_CLAN_IMAGE}/36017218/ab15332ef60d04d3ba061267c9112a6d2712ea78.png

A preview of our new combat system in the works:

 Multiple actions per turn.
 A focus on balancing between attacking and defending.
 Using goods in combat provides different special effects to attacking AND defending.
 Managing enemy intents (are they going to attack or do something else)?
 Guards in the convoy will each have their turns as well.
 Negotiation updates depending on the state of battle (e.g. you may receive a favourable offer to you if you're winning).
 Removed a lot of the randomness from combat with more strategy put back into the player's hands.

Upcoming Improvements

From all the feedback gathered, we will continue to prioritise making significant improvements to the following systems:

 Combat system (currently in progress)
 Wilderness system
 Settlement buildings, interactions, and NPCs
Along with other improvements and updates in the coming months, we will continue to playtest and gather feedback before moving on to more content development.

Until next time,
Cynthia

notes.title: v0.10.2 Development Update - Part 2
notes.notes:
v0.10.2 Combat System Improvements
The follow-up to last month's development blog, here we will go into more detail about the actual improvements to the combat system this build:

Armour & Old Systems
Feedback regarding the previous combat system using the Core / Base attacks was that it overall didn't feel like it added much depth to the combat, and somewhat overcomplicated the system. 

For our improved combat, we have combined the Core / Base system, with the Base now being Enemy Armour. Player attacks will first damage an enemy's armour (with a small amount of the damage hitting their HP) until the enemy's armour breaks. 

{STEAM_CLAN_IMAGE}/36017218/5d47227307b353d7b0be690251c6fbd80a34adde.png
Once the armour is broken, full damage will land on the enemy's HP. Enemy armour will regenerate after a certain amount of turns. The Armour Broken status will have other effects which we will explore with future updated mechanics.

The player wagon now also has Armour, which works very similarly to enemy armour, with the main difference being it won't regenerate after a set number of turns, instead only doing so after each battle. This is also to ease up the game's difficulty as frequent repairs in older game builds caused everything else to be more challenging.

The Finesse and Gambit system switching has also been removed, with their respective combat mechanics divided into Normal Attack and Throwing Goods.

Throwing Goods
The combat system, the fighting itself, has always felt to be the most separated from the merchant gameplay experience, and also the most under-developed as a result. We have added a new mechanic to tie combat closer to trading goods and the merchant experience in general.

{STEAM_CLAN_IMAGE}/36017218/b94e501bd7502e5be3938f44040fa8d9f7acc0c3.png
Players can now throw their trading goods at the enemy, goods which they currently have in their wagon. Each trading good will provide an additional damage bonus on top of basic attack damage, as well as extra effects such as:

 Tools - Causes bleeding for the enemy (take damage each turn)
 Materials - Slightly regenerate wagon armour
 Produce & Food - Remove a beast's armour (the beast is too distracted by the food)

These are just a few examples of the extra effects throwing trading goods will give in combat. Trading goods will now not only affect trading but play an important role in combat as well. Negotiation in combat remains the same, and trading goods are also important there to avoid fighting altogether.

Throwing goods will use the QTE system from the finesse combat style.

{STEAM_CLAN_IMAGE}/36017218/a09ecf2a2540ccbe4293c57835ffa2fa7251629c.png
Thrown goods can be retrieved mid-combat to be used again, but this action will take up a turn. Goods will automatically be retrieved if you win a battle. However, if you run from combat, goods that are not retrieved will be lost forever.

This system plays well into the comedic side of our game, and at the same time, adds a much-needed amount of gameplay depth to the system.

Further improvements to come

 Throwing goods effects - balance each effect to not be over/underpowered
 Item Quality - We will be adding and testing a "Quality" stat added to all goods, and throwing goods in combat will slowly degrade their quality, affecting their value.
 Status Details - Popup details for each enemy's status
 Guards - Update and balance hired guard abilities to work with the improved combat system
 Bug fixes

Content development is still happening in the background alongside these mechanic improvements, so don't worry as overall game development progress is still moving along.

From this point onwards, a bigger focus is put on content creation for the remaining game as well as game balancing and bug fixing.

Featured Updates

Big Optimsation
We have made small optimisation updates with every build thus far, but this build's optimisation will actually be a night and day difference compared with previous builds. 

The game now plays with very minimal loading or lag, especially when changing maps. This was done by frontloading more of the game at the start to reduce on-demand loading times in-game, as well as strictly changing art assets that were heavy on memory use. 

Returning playtesters will notice this difference the most in upcoming playtests!

{STEAM_CLAN_IMAGE}/36017218/7afce89154d6a1aaf4e22cb7d92bac331bb161b4.png

Combat Update - Guards
A follow-up with the previous combat system update, the update in this build now changes how guards/your entire convoy functions in combat.

Old System: 
Selecting one of your guards in the convoy will stack their attack stat on top of your base attack, and striking at your enemy will be a single boosted attack. Your guard will then go into cooldown before being able to be used again.

New System:
Your guards will now attack automatically along with your default crew attack. Attacks are now separate strikes from each source and not a stacked single strike. The cooldown system is therefore not necessary at this time being (unless there are changes to this system in the future).

This change allowed having more guards to have a bigger impact on the player's combat strength, as previously players were still restricted to a single attack per turn, making having more guards a diminishing return. This also includes new sprites and animations to give combat more immersion.

Guard abilities have also been simplified to one notable ability, giving each type of guard your hire a more focused purpose.

{STEAM_CLAN_IMAGE}/36017218/9d89961e1b84dfb8b09766e4cefc07ef7264f14a.png

Our big optimisation has also improved how the wilderness environment art looks and functions, at the same time reducing lag and memory usage.

With so much to implement and update, we have decided to split our big update into two builds: v0.9.0 and v0.9.1. Here is what our first build entails:

Featured Updates

Combat System Update
The combat system has been further expanded, now featuring 2 main types of attacks: Core, and Base. 

Attacking the Core is the same as the normal attack was before, you aim for the enemy's HP. Base, on the other hand, is attacking the enemy's balance. If you deal enough damage to the enemy's Base to reduce it to 0, the enemy will be stunned for a number of turns. 

A stunned enemy cannot attack, loses its abilities (such as armoured or agile), and your escape chance is greatly increased for each stunned enemy (100% escape if all enemies are stunned).

Fighting tougher enemies will require more strategising by attacking their base, then trying to deal as much damage to them while they're stunned. Different guards your hire will also have various abilities which will benefit this new system.

{STEAM_CLAN_IMAGE}/36017218/77c1d0abe006b263c8c3c153da13b6745f1074df.png

Stunning enemies will cause them to lose all abilities for the stun duration, meaning it will be very important to stun tougher enemies with abilities.

New enemy groups also mean new factions to build reputation with.

Hope everyone has had a good start to the new year, despite everything still doing around the world. Here are the updates for Version 0.8.6:

Featured Updates

Combat Styles
A new combat style has been added to provide more gameplay options! Players have been quite divisive with the existing quick-time-event based combat system, either liking it or hating it. Therefore, a new combat style has been added that brings back the RNG/dice roll based combat that existed in earlier builds of this game.

The player can freely switch between the two combat styles (after unlocking them during the tutorial sections). This will allow players to choose when they wish for a quick dice-based battle or to have more control with each attack and defense with quick-time-events. The starting combat style will be the dice-based based combat for simplicity reasons, and other style(s) will be unlocked via tutorials soon into the game.

{STEAM_CLAN_IMAGE}/36017218/ecf324224eb546270ea54b72feadd23646529615.png

Boosts & Penalties
Boosts and Penalties have been added to the game. These are similar to buffs and debuffs found in other games, increasing or decreasing certain stats. These can be acquired in many different ways, some examples are:


 Fatigue - After traveling for 24 hours, the crew will feel fatigued, slightly lowering their combat attack and event success rate.
 Well Rested - Resting in an Inn will remove Fatigue/Exhaustion, providing the Well Rested boost, increasing combat attack and event success rate for 8 hours.
 Prosperous - Obtain this boost after an excellent trade. 


There are many more boosts and penalties, with the possibility of more being added in the future. The old starvation system has also been converted to an indefinite penalty until remedied.

It's here, the big v0.8.0 update! Much of the remaining out-of-date systems have been much improved and revamped, and from this point on, expect new chunks of content with every update!

Featured Updates
Third-person Player and Environment
One of the biggest updates yet to Ten Thousand Coins. The player is able to take control of Viia and explore various settlements, enter buildings, interact with characters and objects. This was a feature planned for a long time and was only implemented in this build to coincide with the new environment art of each settlement.
[previewyoutube=qjCbhW82-o8;full][/previewyoutube]

New Settlement Art and Buildings
The environment assets, especially towns and cities, were some of the oldest art assets dating back to as far as 2017 in the v0.4.x builds. Much of the art is dated, and cramming a miniature settlement on a single screen did not properly represent the atmosphere and feel for each settlement. With the help of our talented artist Elena, each settlement now features a new large map and settlements assets, including buildings to enter. Much had to be updated on the programming side as well, as a new camera system had to implemented to fit with the UI system.
[previewyoutube=8e3P7nyP394;full][/previewyoutube]

Trader Selling and Coin System
In previous builds, it was possible to deposit and convert goods into coins immediately using the coin chest. Upon more testing, we feel this system cut out a bit too much of the trading experience as a merchant, hence the ability to sell goods for coins has to implemented back into the game. As selling goods for coin incurs a certain amount of tax from each trader, the player must also search and sell goods the correct trader to maximize coin return. This system works together with the barter system (still the main trading method to gain a profit) to give the player more strategic choices with trading goods. The coin chest now acts much like a bank term deposit, stores your coins safely to meet milestones.
[previewyoutube=8lBlJWxV5Aw;full][/previewyoutube]

Dialogue and Tutorial System
Behind the scenes work on the tutorial system. While appearing much the same on the surface, the system is now much more optimized with easier management and far fewer instances of gameplay bugs (especially bugs that locked the gameplay indefinitely).
[previewyoutube=LtFW0Q7Ejmg;full][/previewyoutube]

A lot of updates also require a lot of game testing! Next alpha playtesting session coming very soon, stay tuned and remember to sign up for alpha testing at https://www.tenthousandcoins.com !
